item.title: Panama Canal's Real Challenge Is Water, Not Geopolitics
item.description: Almost two years after Donald Trump first threatened to take over the Panama Canal, the storied watershed is thriving.

item.title: Democrats’ Antisemitism Goes Beyond Hasan Piker
item.description: It shouldn’t have taken this long for prominent Democrats to confront their party’s antisemitism problem. But left-wing influencer Hasan Piker apparently crossed a line.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: War, China, Trump and AI Have Created Perma-Crisis
item.description: The struggle for the Strait of Hormuz rages on, new US sanctions threats against Iran notwithstanding. Russian drone and missile strikes punctuate a savage war in Ukraine now approaching its half-decade mark. Fierce competitions afflict regions from East Asia to Eastern Europe. American alliances are in a state of upheaval, while the global economy is fractured by tariffs and sanctions. It seems that nearly every week brings the next AI breakthrough, both promising and portentous.
item.dc:creator: Hal Brands

item.title: Scott Bessent’s Treasury Missteps Threaten Market Confidence
item.description: Putting it mildly, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has had a disappointing month. First, his dubious use of public funds to support Japan’s yen was called in question. Then he embarked on a futile attempt to manipulate the bond market, which led legendary hedge fund manager Stanley Druckenmiller to publicly upbraid his former mentee for the amateurish gambit. item.title: Nepal: The World's Mountains Are Ticking Time Bombs
item.description: From the Apostle Paul to Ira Gershwin, mountains have for millennia been a symbol of immovable stability. A warming planet is undermining that, leaving landslides, floods, and avalanches in its wake.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: London Should Learn From New York's Cannabis Legalization Problems
item.description: There’s a corner near my home in south London where young men gather after dark and smoke marijuana. They often play music and shoot a few hoops. There’s a slightly menacing aspect, but they don’t seem to bother anyone. I certainly don’t sense any furtiveness that would suggest a fear of being reported to the authorities.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: Banks and Insurers Run Risks Playing Shell Games With Credit
item.description: Insurers are doing more to help European banks cut the capital they need to support their loan books. Regulators deliberately opened the door to this — and it’s a choice the authorities may come to regret. Let it run too far, and banks could end up with too little capital when they need it most. There’s also a better answer to this and other problems in European finance: Create deeper capital markets.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Meta Settles Lawsuit for $18 Billion and Now Wants to ‘Support Teens’
item.description: The real test is whether TikTok and YouTube are willing to join the cause.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Is Your Brain Rotted Enough for Microdramas?
item.description: If an alien species learned about humanity solely through microdramas, they would conclude that our lives revolve around spicy secret affairs, billionaire suitors and the occasional werewolf or vampire. There’s a reason I’ve avoided writing about them until now.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: Why Oura and Whoop Are Bound for IPO Glory
item.description: Smart money moves on so fast. The semiconductor stocks that ripped through the roof in the first half of the year are struggling to reclaim momentum. But as a revolutionary technology, the productivity gains from artificial intelligence will be reflected in some asset prices, somehow.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: The Fed’s Dollar Power Comes With a Diplomatic Price
item.description: The ability and willingness of central banks to be forces for global stability will be tested with frequency in coming decades. None is likely to be challenged as much as the Federal Reserve. Such is the burden of the US possessing the world’s primary reserve currency. But is it ready for a more contentious period of statecraft?
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Graham’s South Carolina Win Shows Trump Still Holds His Base
item.description: Darline Graham, sister to former South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham, romped to victory Tuesday over Republican Congressman Ralph Norman, a MAGA conservative, on the strength of her family name and the president’s aggressive push. She now faces Democrat Annie Andrews, a Charleston pediatrician, in the reliably red state.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: US-Canada Tariffs Are a Sideshow to the Real Trade Risks
item.description: After US-Canada trade talks collapsed Friday, the United States imposed a 50% tariff on a long list of Canadian goods via the never-used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer went on TV first thing Monday in an attempt to calm financial markets with some basic tariff math. He said the new action hits a small percentage of Canadian imports into the US and an even smaller share of consumption, so there’s “no possible way it can really affect US well-being.”
item.dc:creator: Scott Lincicome

item.title: Scott Bessent's Bond Moves Won't Get the US Out of Fiscal Trouble
item.description: The US government, steward of the world’s largest economy, faces a darkening fiscal outlook as sovereign borrowing costs surge. Unfortunately, it seems intent on trying any fix except the one that might help.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Bitcoin: The Bessent Bounce Does Not Tell the Full Story
item.description: Bitcoin just notched its biggest weekly gain in more than three years, putting an end to a summer of stagnation. Crypto traders can thank US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose plan to boost bond buybacks spurred the move. But it’ll take more than that to return this market to genuinely bullish territory.
item.dc:creator: Emily Nicolle
